_comment: Pinned third-party targets behind the held-out precision measurement reported in README.md. This file exists because the 2026-07-29 measurement retained no evidence -- no target SHAs, no scan artifacts -- which made a public claim unreproducible. Every target below was re-cloned, re-scanned at the recorded SHA, and every finding hand-audited to ground truth on 2026-07-30. These repo names are already disclosed in README.md; pinning them here adds no new disclosure and is required for the claim to be checkable. Do NOT delete a row when a target moves upstream -- add a new dated block, so the before/after stays meaningful.

measurement.scanner_analysis_note: git diff 2d93061 b508e1c -- mcp_scanner/ is empty: the commits between the 2026-07-29 measurement and this one touched only CI, README frontmatter, and the PyPI distribution name. Zero analysis code changed, so this run is comparable to the 07-29 figures.
measurement.method: Per target: read the detector source to enumerate the real sink list (never assumed), clone upstream at the recorded SHA, run `PYTHONPATH=. python -m mcp_scanner.cli <clone>`, then ground-truth EVERY finding by reading the flagged code and its callers independently of the scanner. A finding counts REAL only if attacker-controlled input can actually reach the sink in a way that matters.

targets.name: notion-mcp-server
targets.pin_note: No commits since 2026-07-25, four days before the measurement. Proves the tip did not move; does not prove the original run pinned the tip, since no SHA was recorded.

targets.name: mcp-server-neon
targets.pin_note: Tip predates the measurement by one day and nothing has landed since.
targets.tools_note: The one detected registration is named '(inline)' -- the regex matched the call but captured no name, because the first argument is a variable.

targets.name: mcp-server-qdrant
targets.pin_note: Zero commits since 2026-06-10, so the state on 07-29 and today are identical.
targets.clean_bill_note: All 15 non-test .py files read plus a grep for the full sink list: zero matches. Both tools route only through qdrant_client's async API. The clean bill is right, not a false negative. This is the only Python target, and the Python precision layer has therefore been correctly silent once and never yet tested against a Python target containing a reachable sink.

targets.name: firecrawl-mcp-server
targets.pin_note: The exact 07-29 pin was unrecorded, so it was bounded instead: all three candidate tips that existed at any point on 2026-07-29 local (a92811a, 7ed0e6b, 7c764ef) produce byte-identical results -- 33 findings, P0=0 P1=12 P2=21. The pin question is moot for this target.

targets.name: airtable-mcp-server
targets.pin_note: Provably the 07-29 state on BOTH sides: the target has not moved since 07-27, and the scanner's analysis code is unchanged since 2d93061.
targets.registration_pattern: current MCP TS SDK: server.registerTool(name, config, handler)
targets.tools_note: _JS_TOOL_RE matches only the DEPRECATED server.tool() API. This repo uses the current registerTool() API in all 16 src/tools/*.ts files.

_recall_note: The 0/53 figure measures PRECISION -- of what was reported, none was real. It says nothing about recall, and the hand audit found real security-relevant issues the scanner missed entirely: an unauthenticated all-interfaces HTTP transport and a committed live-format credential in airtable-mcp-server, an unbounded local file read in firecrawl-mcp-server, and a latent unguarded path read in notion-mcp-server. In two of those cases the scanner OWNS a detector for the class (auth_posture, secret_handling's name-based branch) but gates it on a Python AST and so never runs it on .ts. Do not quote 0/53 as evidence of a clean result on these repos; it is evidence about the findings that were produced, not about the repos.
